Your specific example is complicated by having a double conjunction-clause construct prepended in reverse order and another conjunction, an intransitive verb, and implied subject. The fragment is "whenever something is getting filmed", and would most commonly be appended to the sentence (and is itself an interesting case in reverse subject verb object order with an implied subject by use of the passive voice). Since it is a functionally separate cause, we can ignore it while considering the relative main sentence.

This relative main sentence is "always remember to think about ____ or what is filming it". This also contains a conjoined clause, "about ____ or what is filming it". The clause is the object of inquiry here, but we'll deal with the main sentence first.

The main sentence is "remember to think" (the "always" is a conjunction that is its own clause). The subject is implied (imperative verb "remember", with no subject the is implied to be "you"). It could be written with glossing as:

[You][sub] remember[imp] (to think)[trans], always[conj].

An interesting note is that the imperative mood of the verb is indicated only by the missing implied subject noun, since there is no marker to distinguish the active voice and passive voice of the verb in this case. That is, "you always remember to think" is ambiguous - it could be a description of behavior, or a command to behave a certain way.

Given that understanding of the main sentence and its first conjunction ("remember to think, always"), we can now consider the next conjunction ("____ or what is filming it"). This is a question used as a clause. The subject is a simple conditional ("__ or what"), the verb is "is filming" (two words for the present continuous case make this verb construct), and the subject is "it".

The next fragment is the conjunction-clause "whenever something is getting filmed". The "whenever" is an accessory conjunction to "always" so we drop it and consider the rest of the fragment, "something is getting filmed". Subject "something", verb "is getting filmed". This fragment is fairly complicated to break down too, as one might make a case that the verb is "is getting" and the subject is "filmed", but "filmed" is the primary action, and "is getting" (or, more properly, "is being") is an auxilary component of the verb used to emphasize the present progressive tense of the verb "filmed".

To gloss the whole sentence:

(Whenever[COND] something[SUB] ((is getting)[AUX] filmed)[IMPERF], always[CONJ]) (([you][SUB] remember[IMP] to[part] think[OB]) about[CONJ] ((____ or what)[SUB] (is filming)[PRS] it[OBJ])).

If you used the clause alone as a question, it would be "__ or what is filming it?" Eliminate the selector ("or what") and you're left with: "__ is filming it?" By this point it should be clear that the proper word is "who".

Daily Devotional

May 9

7 The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: because the spirit of the LORD bloweth upon it: surely the people is grass. 8 The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever. (Isaiah 40:7-8 KJV)

This is comparing people with grass, and showing that our bodies are just temporary, as are all matter and plants and animals. If we think of eternity, our whole life on this earth is just for a moment compared to eternity (2 Corinthians 4:17). All material things will pass away in a short time, but the Word of God will last forever (Matthew 24:35). Our souls are spiritual beings, and they will not pass away, but will live forever.

If we stop to ponder these things, it should make us realize that we should value the Word of God more then our own lives. If you have been born again, you will get to spend eternity with God the Father, and Jesus Christ, as well as all the Saints, in Heaven (Revelation 21:27), as long as you don’t blasphemy the Holy Ghost (Matthew 12:31-32), or become reprobate (Romans 1:28), or disobey Jesus (Hebrews 5:9). We should be looking to the future life in Heaven more than worrying about all that is going on in our short lives here on earth. Thank you dear Father, that we will be able to enjoy Your Company forever in the blessings of Heaven.

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
